title: Why phenol is more acidic than ethanol
caption: Phenol (pKa 10.0) loses H⁺ far more readily than ethanol (pKa about 16) because the phenoxide ion's charge is delocalised into the benzene ring. Ethoxide has nowhere to spread its charge.
alt: Phenol in equilibrium with phenoxide, compared with ethanol in equilibrium with ethoxide.
description: Phenol ⇌ phenoxide + H⁺: pKa 10.0, charge spread into the ring.
Ethanol ⇌ ethoxide + H⁺: pKa about 16, charge on oxygen only.
